stories.title: Red Oak’s David Christensen: Industrial Borrowing Remains Consistent
stories.excerpt: The in-person Connect Industrial West 2026 conference, scheduled for Thursday, August 20 at the Hyatt Regency in Irvine, will bring together industry experts to discuss the market’s future direction, new opportunities for West Coast ports and trends in lending. David Christensen, regional manager, West for Red Oak Capital Holdings, will be among the industry leaders taking the stage for “Shifting Capital Flows, Debt, and Valuation Trends in the West.” He provides a preview of the conversation here. Q: From the standpoint of borrowers coming to Red Oak for solutions, has there been a change in the mix of industrial product types they’re focused on, compared to a year ago? Do you see more borrowers looking at outdoor storage sites, for example? A: Not on industrial products; those have been consistent (single, multi-tenant, light manufacturing and flex). We have definitely seen a significant increase in the number of requests for outdoor storage and have so far been lukewarm to the asset class until we can develop a better understanding of the business and long-term viability. The re-use is easy, but that entails a significant decrease in the value that the deal was originally done at. Q: The current administration in Washington has worked to encourage reshoring of manufacturing to the U.S. Has this led to an uptick of borrowers looking to acquire or develop manufacturing facilities? A: Not that we have seen but logically, this has some merit. A lot of the reshoring involves the construction of new facilities, many times in conjunction with a foreign partner versus acquiring an existing property. Q: We’ve seen some lending sources come off the sidelines for the right product type and sponsor. Are you seeing greater competition this year for lending on industrial? bullets: Red Oak Capital reports industrial borrowing demand remains consistent across product types
Significant uptick in outdoor storage inquiries; lender remains cautious on asset class viability
West Coast industrial lending continues stable; no major shift in borrower portfolio focus
stories.summary: Red Oak Capital's Western regional manager reports that industrial borrowing from developers remains steady across traditional product types (single/multi-tenant, light industrial, flex space). However, the firm has seen a marked increase in borrower requests for outdoor storage financing but remains lukewarm on the asset class until business models and long-term durability prove clearer. Industrial debt markets show no significant product-mix disruption compared to a year ago.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is industrial/logistics focused. No direct signal on apartment demand, supply, or capital availability in major multifamily markets.

stories.title: Panattoni Development Company Names Drew Zaborowski Senior Development Manager for Northwest Region
stories.excerpt: Panattoni Development Company has named Drew Zaborowski senior development manager for its Northwest region. In this role, he will help identify and execute new industrial development opportunities while supporting the company’s continued growth throughout the Pacific Northwest. Zaborowski brings more than a decade of experience in industrial real estate development, with expertise spanning site acquisition, due diligence, entitlements, capital structuring, construction management, engineering, and asset dispositions. “We are excited to welcome Drew to the Panattoni team,” said Travis Hale, partner at Panattoni Development Company. “His depth of experience, strategic mindset, and strong understanding of the Northwest market make him an outstanding addition to our team as we continue expanding our presence throughout the region.” Over the past 15 years, Zaborowski has held leadership roles overseeing industrial development projects across the Pacific Northwest. Most recently, he served as a market leader for a logistics property company and later as a co-founder of Bear Creek Real Estate. The post Panattoni Development Company Names Drew Zaborowski Senior Development Manager for Northwest Region appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Panattoni Development names Drew Zaborowski senior development manager for Pacific Northwest
Zaborowski brings 15+ years industrial development expertise; prior roles at logistics and Bear Creek Real Estate
Hire signals Panattoni acceleration of industrial site acquisition and entitlements in Seattle/PNW region
stories.summary: Panattoni Development Company has promoted Drew Zaborowski to senior development manager for its Northwest region, where he will identify and execute new industrial development opportunities. Zaborowski brings over 15 years of experience in industrial real estate development, including site acquisition, due diligence, entitlements, capital structuring, and asset dispositions, with deep ties to the Pacific Northwest market.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Panattoni is primarily industrial/logistics focused; this hire indicates competitive developer activity in the Pacific Northwest but does not directly signal apartment market demand, financing, or cost drivers.

stories.title: Aircraft Finance Firm Buys Florida HQ Complex For $118M
stories.excerpt: A publicly traded aircraft finance firm has paid $118 million for a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Fla. disclosed the transaction and purchase price in a public filing this month. The Coconut Creek-based company bought Cocomar Business Park, under development at 4733, 4763 and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard as its new corporate headquarters, the South Florida Business Journal reported. The company lists its current headquarters as 4700 Lyons Technology Parkway. The seller is an affiliate of Greystar of Charleston, S.C., which last year bought the site for $30.5 million. A marketing brochure said the industrial buildings include 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors and 313 parking spaces. Each building includes a small amount of office space and conference rooms. Completion of the 35-acre campus is expected in the third quarter of this year. In its most recent annual report, Willis Lease Finance said it owns its 60,000-square-foot headquarters in Coconut Creek and leases 45,000 square feet in Pompano Beach, Fla., and 25,000 square feet in Sunrise, Fla. The company reported 475 employees in the U.S., the United Kingdom, Ireland and elsewhere. As of the end of 2025, Willis Lease Finance owned 363 engines, 20 aircraft, one marine vessel and other leased parts and equipment leased out to 69 lessees in 37 countries. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Willis Lease Finance paid $118M for 375K-SF industrial campus in Coconut Creek, Florida for corporate HQ
Greystar acquired site for $30.5M last year; completion expected Q3 2025
32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors, light office/conference space; Willis relocating from two existing Coconut Creek/Pompano sites
stories.summary: Willis Lease Finance, a publicly traded aircraft finance firm, acquired a three-building, 375,000-square-foot industrial complex (Cocomar Business Park) in Coconut Creek, Florida for $118 million as its new corporate headquarters. The Greystar-developed campus, purchased by Greystar in 2024 for $30.5 million, is scheduled for completion in Q3 2025 and includes industrial specs (32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors, 313 parking spaces) alongside office and conference amenities. Willis is consolidating operations from its existing 60,000-square-foot Coconut Creek HQ and 45,000-square-foot Pompano lease.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is industrial/office consolidation in South Florida. However, the $118M acquisition price and Greystar's profitable flip ($30.5M to $118M) suggests strong South Florida industrial and build-to-suit HQ demand, but does not directly impact multifamily apartment supply, demand, or capital markets in the region.

stories.title: Red Sox Consolidate Offices with Three-Floor Lease Near Fenway Park
stories.excerpt: The Boston Red Sox have leased 100,000 square feet at Samuels & Associates’ 1325 Boylston St., a block from Fenway Park, according to published reports. The new location will bring together staff from three locations on an interim basis until delivery begins on the proposed $1.6-billion Fenway Corners mixed-use project. Along with moving Red Sox front-office staff out of Fenway Park, the lease for the top three floors of 1325 Boylston St. will also accommodate parent company Fenway Sports Group and sibling organization Fenway Sports Management. The Boston Business Journal reported that the lease is for six years, with an option to extend it for another five. Long-term, the Major League Baseball franchise plans to occupy a 250,000-square-foot office building that would represent the first phase of Fenway Corners. The team plans to develop the project in partnership with WS Development. A construction timeline has not been announced. Rendering courtesy of CBRE. The post Red Sox Consolidate Offices with Three-Floor Lease Near Fenway Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Boston Red Sox lease 100K SF at 1325 Boylston Street, three floors, near Fenway Park
Six-year lease with five-year extension option; interim home before Fenway Corners $1.6B mixed-use project
Consolidates Red Sox, parent Fenway Sports Group, and FSM staff from three locations; long-term plan includes 250K-SF office building
stories.summary: The Boston Red Sox have leased 100,000 square feet on the top three floors of 1325 Boylston Street, one block from Fenway Park, for a six-year term (with a five-year extension option) to consolidate front-office, parent company (Fenway Sports Group), and sibling organization staff from three existing locations. This is an interim arrangement pending delivery of the first phase of the $1.6 billion Fenway Corners mixed-use development with WS Development, which will include a 250,000-square-foot office building for the franchise. No construction timeline for Fenway Corners has been announced.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is office leasing. However, Fenway Corners is a major mixed-use project in a prime Boston location that will eventually include residential units; the delay in HQ occupancy (interim lease until project delivery) may push residential phasing further out, reducing near-term multifamily supply absorption around Fenway.

stories.title: Retail Real Estate’s Nancy Mozzachio Forms Brokerage Alliance With RJ Brunelli, Expanding Firm’s Presence in PA
stories.excerpt: RJ Brunelli & Co., a Northeast retail real estate brokerage firm, announced a brokerage alliance with industry executive Nancy Mozzachio. In her capacity as a senior consulting broker to Brunelli, Mozzachio will primarily focus on further expanding the firm’s landlord representation platform throughout southern New Jersey and Pennsylvania markets. Additionally, the brokerage formed a strategic relationship with Mozzachio’s Sine Qua Non Real Estate Advisors, a New Jersey-based firm that provides development and operations services to retail and mixed-use developers, property owners and investors. The firm also provides economic development consulting services for municipalities. Mozzachio brings more than three decades of leadership in retail real estate leasing, redevelopment, and operations, having represented institutional and private ownership throughout her career. “We are excited about the opportunities this relationship creates for our presence throughout New Jersey and Pennsylvania,” said Danielle Brunelli, president and principal of RJ Brunelli & Co. The post Retail Real Estate’s Nancy Mozzachio Forms Brokerage Alliance With RJ Brunelli, Expanding Firm’s Presence in PA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RJ Brunelli retail brokerage forms alliance with veteran broker Nancy Mozzachio
Mozzachio's Sine Qua Non Real Estate Advisors provides development/operations services to retail and mixed-use projects
Alliance expands landlord representation and municipal economic development services across Pennsylvania and New Jersey
stories.summary: Northeast retail brokerage RJ Brunelli & Co. has formed a brokerage alliance with senior consulting broker Nancy Mozzachio and her firm, Sine Qua Non Real Estate Advisors, a New Jersey-based development and operations advisory firm serving retail and mixed-use developers, property owners, and municipalities. The alliance is designed to expand Brunelli's landlord representation platform throughout southern New Jersey and Pennsylvania and strengthen municipal economic development services.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is retail-focused brokerage activity. No signal on apartment demand, supply, or capital markets.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $23M for Apartments in Federal Way
stories.excerpt: Andy Slaton, senior vice president, and John Holt, senior investment analyst, of Northmarq’s San Francisco Debt and Equity team arranged the $23.25 million refinance of Align Apartments, a 105-unit multifamily property located at 35434 25th Ave SW in Federal Way, Washington. Northmarq canvassed the market on behalf of the borrower, St. Regis Properties, including life company and debt fund executions, and ultimately structured the transaction through its correspondent relationship with Voya Investment Management. The floating-rate bridge loan was structured with a four-year term, full-term interest-only payments and flexible prepayment. Built in 1991 and renovated by the current ownership, Align Apartments consists of 11 three-story buildings totaling 107,448 square feet on 6.33 acres. The unit mix includes 63 two-bedroom and 42 three-bedroom units. Community amenities include a pool, fitness center, clubhouse, playground and dog park. Since acquiring the property in 2022, the sponsor has invested approximately $2.1 million in interior and exterior capital improvements. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Northmarq Arranges $23M for Apartments in Federal Way appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $23.25M floating-rate bridge refinance for Align Apartments, Federal Way, Washington
105-unit property (63 two-bed, 42 three-bed); built 1991, renovated; four-year term, interest-only, full prepayment flexibility
Borrower St. Regis Properties invested $2.1M in capital improvements since 2022 acquisition
stories.summary: Northmarq's San Francisco Debt and Equity team arranged a $23.25 million floating-rate bridge refinance for Align Apartments, a 105-unit multifamily property in Federal Way, Washington, on behalf of borrower St. Regis Properties. The loan features a four-year term with full-term interest-only payments and flexible prepayment, structured through Voya Investment Management. The property, built in 1991 and recently renovated with $2.1 million in capital improvements, comprises 11 three-story buildings (63 two-bedroom, 42 three-bedroom units) with community amenities including pool, fitness center, and dog park.
stories.impact: Federal Way, WA: Bridge financing availability for stabilized multifamily assets remains accessible; floating-rate execution with 4-year term reflects current debt market appetite for well-maintained, value-add properties in Seattle-area suburbs. Capital availability supports hold-and-improve strategies but floating rates signal borrowers still exposed to rate volatility—likely constraining aggressive new development starts in the submarket.

stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach assisted living facility to Artemis Real Estate Partners for $140M+
224K-SF, 207-unit community completed 2023; includes 35.6K-SF clubhouse and 51.5K-SF nursing; $676.3K per unit
Artemis acquisition signals strong South Florida senior housing market; PGIM exited after ~2-year hold post-completion
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach, a 224,951-square-foot assisted living community with 207 units, to Artemis Real Estate Partners for at least $140 million, marking one of South Florida's largest senior housing sales in recent years. The property, completed by PGIM in 2023 on a 7.2-acre site, includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and 51,461-square-foot nursing facility. The transaction values the asset at approximately $676,300 per unit. PGIM-backed Alliance Residential had purchased the land for $8.2 million in 2021 and secured a $45.7 million construction loan.
stories.impact: Delray Beach, South Florida: Senior housing asset sale at premium multiples and rapid exit (2-year hold) signals strong investor appetite for age-restricted/assisted living communities in South Florida, likely driven by demographic migration and robust occupancy. This capital activity may crowd out traditional multifamily development capital in the region and indicates alternative residential products are outperforming conventional apartments on yield, potentially affecting multifamily development feasibility in the submarket.

stories.title: Mamdani Invests $8.4M in Business Improvement Districts Citywide
stories.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is upping the grant funding available to local organizations that promote commerce — though it doesn’t look like much. Mamdani and the New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) is making $8.4 million available to business improvement districts for public art displays, street cleaning, lighting and directories. While $8.4 million might not be the most impressive figure, the administration says it could boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses in the five boroughs, and is the largest single cash infusion of its kind. “Our administration knows it’s not enough to make it easier to open a small business, you have to make it easier to visit one, too,” Mamdani said in a statement. “That’s why our commitment to small businesses means not only cutting red tape and reducing fines, but investing in the neighborhoods surrounding bodegas, bookshops and restaurants so that New York City is lined with ‘OPEN’ signs year-round.” The grant money has already been awarded, with Brooklyn taking the majority of available funding, or $2.7 million for 32 organizations, while 17 entities in the Bronx received $1.55 million, according to the administration. Manhattan and Queens received similar amounts, while the Bronx saw less funding and Staten Island got the least: $550,000 to only seven organizations. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Mayor Mamdani allocates $8.4M in grants to Business Improvement Districts citywide
Funding supports public art, street cleaning, lighting, directories; expected to boost foot traffic to 20K businesses
Largest single BID cash infusion to date; Brooklyn receives largest share
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Department of Small Business Services are distributing $8.4 million in grant funding to Business Improvement Districts across all five boroughs for public art installations, street cleaning, lighting improvements, and business directories. The administration estimates the investment will drive foot traffic to approximately 20,000 businesses and represents the largest single cash infusion of its kind to BIDs. Brooklyn receives the largest allocation.
stories.impact: New York City: Small public investment in streetscape and BID infrastructure is a modest demand signal for foot-traffic-dependent neighborhoods, but $8.4M is minimal relative to NYC's economy and multifamily development pipeline. No material impact on apartment demand, supply, or capital markets. Could support retail activation in emerging residential neighborhoods (e.g., Sunset Park, Astoria) but insufficient to drive material rental demand by itself.

stories.title: Developer Plans 297 Housing Units Across From Downtown Brooklyn Macy’s Project
stories.excerpt: Another residential tower might be coming to Downtown Brooklyn, directly across from a major retail makeover project at the former Macy’s. Local developer Shimon Klein has filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings to bring a trio of 99-unit residential buildings along Fulton Street between Bridge and Lawrence streets. The 99-unit nature of the filing means Klein will likely try to utilize the city’s controversial 485-x tax abatement program, which comes with a construction wage requirement for projects with 100 or more units. Klein’s proposal calls for a 99-unit, 27-story building at 485 Fulton Street. The registered architect is Kao Hwa Lee from Kao Hwa Lee Architects. Neither the architect nor the developer responded to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building at 485 Fulton Street would have between four and eight residential units across the third through 27th floors. There would also be commercial and community facility space, as well as nearly 3,000 square feet of outdoor rooftop space for tenants. There are no further amenity details, but offerings including workout space, communal lounges, and coworking options have become non-negotiables in new residential developments. The other two 99-unit buildings would be built at 147 and 149 Lawrence Street, with similar makeups, according to the filing. The tenants of Klein’s new project would have a plethora of entertainment options in the neighborhood. The building is located across the street from 422 Fulton Street, a former Macy’s department store, which is being renovated into a five-floor retail and entertainment spot called BKX, CO previously reported. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Developer Shimon Klein files plans for 99-unit residential tower at 485 Fulton Street, Downtown Brooklyn
27-story building designed to avoid 100-unit wage requirement; 99 units across floors 3-27; commercial/CF/rooftop space
Positioned across from $1.6B Macy's retail conversion; utilizes 485-x tax abatement program
stories.summary: Local developer Shimon Klein has filed plans with NYC Department of Buildings for a 99-unit residential building at 485 Fulton Street in Downtown Brooklyn, directly across from a major Macy's conversion project. The 27-story tower is designed to deliberately keep unit count at 99 to avoid the 100-unit construction wage requirement. The proposal includes commercial and community facility space, with rooftop tenant space totaling nearly 3,000 square feet. Klein is pursuing the city's 485-x tax abatement program.
stories.impact: Downtown Brooklyn: The 99-unit filing signals developer activity and tax-abatement arbitrage near major retail reactivation (Macy's conversion), suggesting confidence in demand fundamentals. However, the deliberate cap at 99 units to avoid wage escalation reflects tight development economics and labor-cost sensitivity in the submarket—flag this as a cost headwind reducing project feasibility at 100+ units. Retail makeover may drive foot traffic and rental appeal, supporting multifamily demand, but delivery timing and financing remain unclear.

stories.title: Payments Manager Corpay Cross-Border Relocates to 18K SF at 560 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: An international payment and currency risk management firm is planning a headquarters relocation to Rudin’s 560 Lexington Avenue. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which operates under corporate payments company Corpay, has signed an 11-year lease for 17,778 square feet at the Plaza District tower, Commercial Observer has learned. The landlord declined to provide the asking rent, but an April lease inside Rudin’s 22-story tower asked $84 per square foot, according to previous CO reports. Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay, while Rudin was represented in-house by Kevin Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. Corpay Cross-Border plans to move from Tishman Speyer‘s 300 Park Avenue into its new, prebuilt office, which occupies the entire 17th floor of 560 Lexington, this fall. Daly, Rudin’s vice president of office leasing, stated that the deal validates recent portfolio investments, which allowed for minimal modifications to meet Corpay’s space requirements. “This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done,” Daly said. Located two blocks from Grand Central Terminal, the 380,000-square-foot office building at the corner of Lexington Avenue and East 50th Street has seen over 91,000 square feet of leasing activity in the last six months, according to Rudin. Recent arrivals include financial firm Marex, hedge fund SummitTX and coworking firm Industrious. Spokespeople for CBRE and Corpay Cross-Border did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions signed 11-year lease for 17.8K SF at 560 Lexington Avenue, Midtown Manhattan
Relocating from 300 Park Avenue; lease at $84/SF asking rate; occupies full 17th floor
Move-in fall 2025; Rudin's minimal buildout confirms pre-built office strategy and landlord infrastructure investment
stories.summary: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, an international payment and currency risk management firm, has signed an 11-year lease for 17,778 square feet at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue in Midtown Manhattan's Plaza District, with move-in slated for fall 2025. The tenant is relocating from Tishman Speyer's 300 Park Avenue. The lease was executed at approximately $84 per square foot (asking rate), and the space occupies the entire 17th floor with minimal buildout required due to Rudin's pre-built office strategy.
stories.impact: Midtown Manhattan office: A capital-intensive financial services firm choosing Midtown and committing to an 11-year lease signals modest confidence in office space demand and economic activity in the Plaza District, but this is a single large-floor lease and does not indicate broader office market recovery. For multifamily development in Midtown/Midtown East: office consolidation and landlord investment in pre-built space may support worker concentration and nearby residential demand, but no direct signal on apartment supply or capital availability.
